## Which EO Platform?

- Google Earth Engine (GEE)
- Microsoft Planetary Computer (MPC)
- Earth on AWS 
- Sentinel Hub 
- OpenEO 
- Open Data Cube (ODC)
- SEPAL 
- JEODPP 
- pipsCloud 

::: {.notes}
Over the years, a large number of EO-Platforms have emerged.
I find the openEO plattform to be especially promising
:::

## Platform Overview

Gomes et al. (2020): An Overview of Platforms for Big Earth Observation Data Management and Analysis

[https://doi.org/10.3390/rs12081253](https://doi.org/10.3390/rs12081253)

(outdated)

::: {.notes}
MPC and AWS missing!
:::

## OpenEO

![](images/openeo_logo.png)

openEO develops an open API to connect R, Python, JavaScript and other clients to big Earth observation cloud back-ends in a simple and unified way.

::: {.notes}
OpenEO:
- is an open source project
- provides a standardized API (is a wrapper around existing plattforms)
- this adds a layer of additional complexity
- for, is best accessed via the R API which obfuscates the "cloud" aspect
:::

## Platform Comparison

> ...most people prefer GEE mostly because it's the good ol' reliable when it comes to EO data on the cloud. Mature, well-documented and a huge community. 
> 
> MPC is the new kid on the block, they provide a more bare-bone version of GEE, with the added advantage of connecting your own computing environment on Azure.

[source](https://www.reddit.com/r/remotesensing/comments/16cddfa/confused_on_the_big_data_platforms/)

## Getting Started

4. Follow along! (Demo time)

::: {.notes}
Walk through the code in `01-browser-console-demo.md`

## Recap

## Variable Declaration

```javascript
// Variables are used to store objects, and are defined
// using the keyword var.
var the_answer = 42;

// String objects start and end with double quotes.
var my_variable = "I am a string";
```

```javascript
// there are other ways to declare variables in js
let the_answer = 42;
const the_answer = 42;
// we will ignore these
```

## Statements

```javascript
// Statements *should* end in a semi-colon
var test = 'I feel incomplete...'

var test = 'I feel complete...';
```

## HTML Script Setup

1. Open a **plain text editor**
2. Create a file with the extension `.html`
3. Create a `script` tag

```html
<script>

</script>
```

4. Open this file in the browser
5. Follow along! (Demo time)

::: {.notes}
walk through the script `02-basic-html-script-demo.md`
:::

## Recap

## Comments

```javascript
// Line comments start with two forward slashes.
// Like this line.

/*
Multi line comments start with a forward slash
and a star,
and end with a star and a forward slash.
*/
```

## Arrays

```javascript
// Square brackets are used to create a list of items
var my_list = ['eggplant', 'apple', 'wheat'];

// Square brackets are also used for selecting items within
// a list. 0 refers to the first item in the list.
my_list[0];
```

## Dictionaries

```javascript
// Curly brackets are used to define "dictionaries"
var my_dict = {'food':'bread', 'color':'red', 'number':42};

// Square brackets are used to access items (by key).
my_dict['color'];

// Or you can use the dot notation to get the same result.
my_dict.color;
```

## Functions

```javascript
// Functions can be defined as a way to reuse code and
// make it easier to read.
function years2days(years){
    return years*365
};

years2days(34);
```

## Functions (Alternative Syntax)

```javascript
// Functions can be defined as a way to reuse code and
// make it easier to read.
var say_hello = function(string) {
    return 'Hello ' + string + '!';
};

say_hello('world');
```

Your task for this afternoon:

1. Reimplement one of the demonstrated analyses to a different area (or implement your own idea)

# Graded Assignment {data-background-image="images/sunflowers-8980921_1280.jpg"}

## Assignment Details

Apply the expertise and skills you acquire within the two remote sensing sessions to design and elaborate your own research project. Make sure to describe the motivation, a suitable analysis approach and applicable remote sensing data.

The short research proposal is not to exceed 1 page and can include one figure.

Deadline is one week after the final session of the remote sensing input (2.10.2025)
